question: Explain the scheme of Advance Pricing Agreements (APA) under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
sources: Income-tax Rules, 1962, rules 10F to 10T (advance pricing agreement rules)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: The Board, with the approval of the Central Government, may enter into an agreement with any person determining the arm's length price, or the method of determining it, for an international transaction that person will enter into.

points.label: Types of APA
points.description: An APA may be unilateral (between the taxpayer and the Indian tax authority), or bilateral or multilateral (also involving the tax authorities of other countries through the mutual agreement procedure).
points.basis: Income-tax Rules, 1962, advance pricing agreement rules (definitions of unilateral, bilateral and multilateral agreements)

points.label: Period and rollback
points.description: An APA is valid for the period it specifies, not exceeding five consecutive previous years; it may also be rolled back to apply to international transactions of up to four earlier previous years.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 92CC (validity period) and section 92CC(9A) (rollback)

points.label: Binding effect
points.description: The agreement binds the person and the income-tax authorities for the transactions it covers, but stops binding if the law or facts on which it was based change.

points.label: Void agreements and modified return
points.description: An APA obtained by fraud or misrepresentation of facts is void from the start. Where returns for covered years were already filed, the person files a modified return in line with the APA within the prescribed time, and assessment is made on that basis.
